card.occupation: Dental technician at a small independent dental laboratory in the town, making crowns, bridges and partial dentures to order for local practices. She has done this for over 25 years.
card.education_detail: Left secondary school at 16 with a handful of O levels. She did a BTEC in dental technology through day release at college while working as a trainee at the lab, and has kept up her registration and CPD since.
card.household: Lives on her own in a two-bedroom terraced house she bought in her early thirties. She has no pets now; her cat died two years ago and she hasn't had the heart to get another yet. Her widowed mum lives about ten minutes away, and Denise goes round most days.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in St Helens in a working-class family. Her dad worked at the glassworks and her mum was a school dinner lady. Brought up Church of England, she still goes to her local parish church most Sundays, helps with the flower rota and does teas after services now and then. Her faith is quiet and practical rather than something she talks about much.
card.professional_persona: Careful, patient and precise. She takes real pride in getting a fit right first time and hates the idea of sending out something that isn't up to scratch. The dentists trust her because she'll ring and say if an impression isn't good enough rather than bodge it. She's not interested in managing people or chasing work; she likes her bench, her radio and getting on with it. She's quietly irritated when corners get cut to save money.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself, but she walks a lot, mainly around Taylor Park and the canal, and does a gentle aqua class once a week at the leisure centre. She follows rugby league loosely because her dad was a Saints fan, and she'll watch a big match on telly with her mum.
card.arts_persona: Enjoys a good crime drama or period piece on the telly, reads library books, mostly cosy mysteries and family sagas, and sings in the church choir at Christmas and Easter. She went to the Theatre Royal in St Helens to see a touring musical last year and loved it, though she'd never go on her own.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are modest and familiar. There's a week in North Wales or the Lake District most years, sometimes with her mum, sometimes with an old school friend. She's been abroad a few times, to Majorca and once on a coach tour of Austria with a church group, but she gets anxious about flying and airports and prefers a caravan or a B&B within driving distance.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking. She makes a big pan of scouse or a stew on a Sunday and has it through the week, does a roast for her mum, and likes a chippy tea on a Friday. She's a decent baker and does scones and a Victoria sponge for church events. A barm with chips or a bacon barm is her idea of a treat.
hobbies_and_interests: walking by the canal and in local parks
watching quiz shows and detective dramas
keeping her small back yard tidy with pots of geraniums
doing word searches and the crossword in the paper
skills: fine manual dexterity and detailed model work
looking after an elderly parent: appointments, medication, paperwork
card.career_goals: No big ambitions. She'd like to keep working at the lab until she can retire at around 63 or 65, and hopes the place doesn't get bought out by one of the big chains. She'd maybe like to train up the young lad who's started there so the skills don't get lost.
card.voice: Soft-spoken, a bit hesitant at first, with a mild St Helens accent that sits somewhere between Wigan and Liverpool without being strong. She speaks at a steady, unhurried pace and uses 'erm' when she's thinking. She hedges a lot, with 'sort of', 'I suppose' and 'I don't know really', and apologises easily ('sorry, I've gone off on one there'). She says 'tea' for her evening meal and 'barm' for a roll, and might say 'give it me' without noticing. Silences make her a little uneasy, so she'll often fill them with a small qualifier or ask 'is that what you wanted?' She warms up and gets chattier once she feels she's not saying the wrong thing.
card.typing: Types carefully but briefly. She usually capitalises the first word and puts a full stop at the end, and gets apostrophes right most of the time. She doesn't use abbreviations or emojis, and might occasionally type 'not sure' or 'depends really'. Answers are short and honest rather than elaborate, sometimes with an extra clause added to be fair, like 'Sometimes, but not always.'
card.with_strangers: Polite, reserved and a bit nervous to begin with. She doesn't like being the centre of attention and worries about giving the 'right' answer, but she's genuinely kind and very straight. She won't exaggerate or show off, and will correct herself if she thinks she's overstated something. Once she's comfortable she's warm, gently funny and very easy to talk to.
small_things: her mum's latest hospital appointment or what the doctor said
the price of things at Asda going up again
the weather being miserable or the nights drawing in
a jigsaw she's halfway through on the dining table
what she's having for her tea
a programme she's been watching on catch-up
the coffee morning at church and who brought what
deeper_things: She sometimes wonders whether she should have married or had children. There was someone in her twenties, but it didn't work out, and she doesn't regret it exactly but thinks about it.
She worries about what will happen when her mum can't manage on her own, and feels the weight of being the only one nearby since her brother moved to Devon.
She still misses her dad, who died eight years ago, and gets teary around his birthday.
She gets lonely in the evenings more than she lets on, especially since losing her cat.
Her faith helped her a lot after her dad died, and she finds comfort in the routine of church even when she's not sure what she believes about everything.
card.webcam_photo: A slightly low-angle webcam shot from a laptop on a dining table, framing her from the shoulders up, a little off-centre to the left. The room is lit by a ceiling light and some greyish daylight from a window out of frame on the right, so her face is evenly but flatly lit. She is a white woman in her early fifties with a round, kind face, light lines around her eyes and a polite, slightly unsure closed-mouth smile. Her hair is shoulder-length, mid-brown with some grey coming through at the parting, tucked behind one ear. She wears thin gold-rimmed reading glasses and a lilac knitted cardigan over a plain white top, with a small gold cross on a chain just visible at her neck. Behind her is a magnolia-painted wall with a framed print of a lakeside scene, a wooden display cabinet holding a few china ornaments and photo frames, and the edge of a half-finished jigsaw puzzle on the table near the bottom of the frame.
